name: Báciga
description: Báciga is the distinct Uruguayan evolution of the Spanish fishing game 'Escoba'. While it retains the core mechanic of capturing cards that sum to 15, Báciga adds a layer of 'declarations' (hand combinations) similar to Poker or Rummy. Points are scored through table captures, 'Escobas' (clearing the table), and special three-card combos like the 'Chorizo'. It is widely celebrated in Uruguay as a faster, more combo-driven alternative to Truco.

history.origins: Derived from the Spanish game 'Escoba de 15' which was brought to South America by immigrants. In Uruguay, it merged with elements of the game 'Chorizo' to become the modern Báciga.
timeline: 1800s: Escoba introduced to the Rio de la Plata region.
Early 20th Century: 'Chorizo' variant emerges in Uruguay with point-heavy hand declarations.
1950s: Báciga rules stabilize as a 'lite' version of Chorizo, becoming a staple in Uruguayan 'clubes sociales'.
Present: One of the 'Big Two' traditional card games in Uruguay alongside Truco.
history.cultural: In Uruguay, Báciga is often played over coffee or matte, known for its rapid-fire arithmetic and the dramatic 'cantar' (announcement) of hand bonuses.
history.evolution: The game moved from a simple arithmetic capture game to a high-scoring strategy game where a single 'Chorizo' (three-of-a-kind) can end the session.

setup.players: 2-4 players. 4-player games are usually partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.dealing: 1. Dealer deals 3 cards to each player face down. 2. 4 cards are dealt face up to the table. 3. Dealing is counter-clockwise.
setup.equipment: Standard Spanish deck, pen and paper for 21-point tracking.

rules.objective: Be the first to reach 21 points through captures and hand declarations.
rules.gameplay: 1. Dealer gives 3 cards to each player, 4 face-up on table. 2. Declaration phase: players may announce Chorizo, Flor, Báciga, or Escalera before play. 3. In turn, each player plays one card to capture table cards that sum to 15, or adds a card to the table. 4. Escoba: capturing all table cards scores bonus. 5. When hands empty, dealer deals 3 more cards; repeat until deck exhausted. 6. Score: Oros (coins), Cartas (cards), Setenta (sevens). First to 21 wins.
keyRules: The 7 of Coins is the most valuable individual card.
If the initial 4 cards on the table sum to 15 or 30, the Dealer takes them as 1 or 2 Escobas immediately.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the 7 of Coins. Try to avoid leaving the table with a sum that allows an easy '15' for the next player.
strategy.intermediate: Table Management: If you can't take a trick, play a card that makes the table total difficult to combine into 15 (e.g., if the table has a 4, don't play an Ace if you know the opponent has a 10/Sota).
strategy.advanced: Communication (Partnerships): Use your lead to signal the suit of your 'Flor' or 'Escalera' to your partner without explicitly saying it.
tips: Winning the 'Setenta' (best sevens) is often the tie-breaker in close games.
If you are close to 21, focus on 'Escobas'���they are the fastest way to move the dial.

variations.name: Chorizo (Traditional)
variations.description: The 'parent' game where the declaration values are much higher and the session usually goes to 31 points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Chorizo is documented here as background; full rule differences will be modeled in its own game entry.

scoring.description: Accumulative points across multiple deals until 21 is reached.

synthesis.shortDescription: Dive into Uruguay's favorite arithmetic challenge. Báciga is a sophisticated fishing game where every card's mathematical value matters. Build the perfect hand to 'cantar' your points and sweep the table clean to become the 21-point champion.

hero.title: BÁCIGA
hero.subtitle: The Soul of Uruguay
hero.tagline: Capture the table. Declare the Flor. And hope for the Chorizo that wins it all.
